lesson.title: Clear up the plan
lesson.scenario: Knafeh and Fattoush arrange a visit to Knafeh’s family tomorrow at seven in the evening. Fattoush initially hears six. Use brief corrections and a final confirmation; later practice changes the details.

steps.instruction: Fattoush heard six. As Knafeh, correct her: the visit is at seven.

answers.rationale: This directly corrects six to seven.
This repeats the mistaken six instead of correcting it.
Tomorrow may fit, but it does not resolve the mistaken time.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This directly corrects six to seven.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: Knafeh corrected the time. Confirm tomorrow at seven and visiting HIS family.

answers.meaning: Tomorrow at seven we’ll visit my family.
answers.rationale: As Fattoush, ahli would change the visit to her own family.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة سبعة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at seven we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This preserves tomorrow and seven; ahlak refers to Knafeh’s family.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This restores the mistaken time of six.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This preserves tomorrow and seven; ahlak refers to Knafeh’s family.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.
evaluation.retryHint: Keep seven and your listener’s family.

steps.instruction: New misunderstanding: Fattoush checks “today?” You mean tomorrow. Correct only the day.

answers.rationale: This supplies seven but leaves the day unclear.

answers.arabic: اليوم الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Il-yōm is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Today at six we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This confirms the mistaken today and invents a time.

evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: Transfer: the agreed visit is now at SIX tomorrow. As Fattoush, correct Knafeh when he says seven.

answers.rationale: This corrects the time to the new intended six.
This keeps seven, which is wrong for this new arrangement.
Tomorrow is already agreed; the mistake is the time.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This corrects the time to the new intended six.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: Continue the new six-o’clock arrangement. Knafeh says “my family.” Confirm tomorrow at six and HIS family.

prompt.meaning: Shall we visit my family after work?

answers.meaning: Tomorrow at seven we’ll visit my family.
answers.rationale: This changes both the time and whose family will be visited.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة ستة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sitte nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at six we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This preserves the new six-o’clock time and refers to Knafeh’s family.

answers.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة سبعة نزور أهلك.
answers.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nzūr ahlak.
answers.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at seven we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This carries over seven from the old plan.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This preserves the new six-o’clock time and refers to Knafeh’s family.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.

steps.instruction: New activity: Fattoush asks about tomorrow. Agree to tea together at seven, with no family visit in this plan.

answers.meaning: Tomorrow at seven we’ll visit my family.
answers.rationale: Seven fits, but the family visit is not part of this arrangement.

answers.arabic: بكرا الساعة ستة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Bukra is-sāʿa sitte nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Tomorrow at six we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: Tea fits, but six changes the requested time.

answers.arabic: آه، بكرا الساعة سبعة نشرب شاي سوا.
answers.arabizi: Āh, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nishrab shāy sawa.
answers.meaning: Yes, tomorrow at seven we’ll drink tea together.
answers.rationale: This confirms exactly the new day, time and activity.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This confirms exactly the new day, time and activity.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This expression changes or omits a detail requested in this exchange.
evaluation.retryHint: Check all three: day, time, activity.

introduction.goal: Correct a misunderstood time or day and confirm whose family you will visit.

line.meaning: Tomorrow at seven we’ll visit my family.

line.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة سبعة نزور أهلك.
line.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nzūr ahlak.
line.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at seven we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)
And afterwards we’ll drink tea together.

expressions.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة سبعة نزور أهلك.
expressions.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nzūr ahlak.
expressions.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at seven we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)

introduction.usageNote: A short laʾ plus the corrected detail can repair a misunderstanding. Keep the correction about the mistaken detail, then confirm the full plan. These are bounded exchanges, not a universal politeness rule.
introduction.dialectNote: Urban Palestinian teaching target; transliteration remains available. Urban coffee pronunciation and address forms follow the first-unit model. Ahlak addresses Knafeh; ahli refers to the speaker’s own family. The scenes share an evening setting; these phrases do not teach how to distinguish morning from evening. No Jordanian variants or native-expert review claimed. ā/ī/ū and ē/ō mark long vowels; ʿ = ع, ḥ = ح, ʾ = glottal stop.
introduction.recordingNote: No reviewed recordings. Dialogue and prompt text are draft recording scripts. Speaker roles are explicit; do not label browser speech as reviewed Palestinian audio. All audio URLs remain null.

teachingCards.title: Check what you heard
teachingCards.note: The question repeats the time to check it. Its intonation differs from a statement; no reviewed audio is available yet.
teachingCards.recallCue: You think you heard six. Check that time.

teachingCards.title: Repair the time
teachingCards.note: Laʾ rejects the repeated six; is-sāʿa sabʿa gives the intended time.
teachingCards.recallCue: Fattoush heard six, but you meant seven. Correct the time.

teachingCards.title: Repair the day
teachingCards.note: When the question is about today, laʾ, bukra corrects only the day.
teachingCards.recallCue: Someone checks “today?” You mean tomorrow. Correct them.

teachingCards.title: Confirm from the listener’s perspective

phrase.arabic: تمام، بكرا الساعة سبعة نزور أهلك.
phrase.arabizi: Tamām, bukra is-sāʿa sabʿa nzūr ahlak.
phrase.meaning: Okay, tomorrow at seven we’ll visit your family. (to Knafeh)

teachingCards.note: Knafeh says ahli, my family. Fattoush says ahlak, your family, to refer to those same people.
teachingCards.recallCue: Confirm to Knafeh: tomorrow at seven, visit his family.

chunks.meaning: we visit your family · to Knafeh

teachingCards.title: Use the actual new time
teachingCards.note: Do not memorize seven as the right answer. A different arrangement can require six.
teachingCards.recallCue: New plan: the intended time is six, not seven. Correct the time.
